citation_reference: Müller (2015), Ch. 1, p. 14
claim_text: In 12-TET with A4=440 Hz reference, middle C (C4) has frequency f(60) = 440 * 2^((60-69)/12) ≈ 261.63 Hz.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Fails if reference frequency is not 440 Hz (e.g. historical A=432 Hz or 415 Hz) or tuning is non-equal temperament.

citation_reference: Müller (2015), Ch. 2, p. 42
claim_text: Pitch classes are defined by modulo 12 equivalence of MIDI note numbers, partitioning all pitches into 12 equivalence classes {0, 1, ..., 11}.
musical_example: MIDI 12, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84 all belong to pitch class 0 (C).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Fails in microtonal or non-12-EDO systems (e.g. 19-EDO, 24-EDO, 31-EDO).

citation_reference: Walker (1996), I.4–I.5, https://www.mtosmt.org/issues/mto.96.2.6/mto.96.2.6.walker.html Historical reference: Prehn (2017), Sec. 1.2, p. 8 (unverified).
claim_text: Pythagorean tuning builds fifths at 3:2. Twelve pure fifths exceed seven octaves by the Pythagorean comma, approximately 23.46 cents.
musical_example: (3/2)^12 / 2^7 = 531441/524288. A fifth is approximately 701.955 cents.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The exact comma compares twelve pure fifths with seven exact 2:1 octaves. In 12-TET the fifth is exactly 700 cents.

citation_reference: Wibberley (2004), paragraph 20 and the preceding calculation, https://www.mtosmt.org/retrofit/mto.04.10.1/mto.04.10.1.wibberley1.php Historical reference: Prehn (2017), Sec. 2.1, p. 19 (unverified).
claim_text: In a 5-limit just triad the major third can be 5:4, the minor third 6:5 and the perfect fifth 3:2.
musical_example: A just C-major triad can use 1:1, 5:4, 3:2. A just C-minor triad can use 1:1, 6:5, 3:2.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: These are ratios in individual triads. A fixed set of pitches need not realize these ratios in every key.

citation_reference: Scholtz (1998), §§6.1–6.4, https://www.mtosmt.org/issues/mto.98.4.4/mto.98.4.4.scholtz.html Historical reference: Prehn (2017), Sec. 3.4, p. 35 (unverified).
claim_text: Quarter-comma meantone narrows regular fifths by one quarter of the syntonic comma, about 5.38 cents, to about 696.58 cents. Four such fifths reduced by two octaves give a pure major third of 5:4.
musical_example: (3/2)^4 / (81/80) / 2^2 = 5/4. Closing a 12-note chain of 11 regular fifths leaves a wolf fifth of about 737.64 cents.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The wolf placement depends on the chosen 12-note chain. The narrowed regular fifth applies to the chain, not to its closing interval.

citation_reference: Benson (2006), §5.11, Werckmeister III diagram, https://www.lpthe.jussieu.fr/~talon/MUSIC5.PDF Historical reference: Prehn (2017), Sec. 4.1, p. 48 (unverified).
claim_text: Werckmeister III narrows C–G, G–D, D–A and B–F# by one quarter of the Pythagorean comma each. The other fifths in the circle are pure.
musical_example: The major third C–E spans about 390.225 cents; F#–A# spans about 407.820 cents in the 12-note layout where A# shares the Bb key.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The intervals are properties of the specified temperament. Perceived key character is a separate question.

citation_reference: Hindemith (1944), Ch. 1, p. 12
claim_text: Acoustic interval dissonance order ranks octave > fifth > fourth > major third/sixth > minor third/sixth > major second/minor seventh > minor second/major seventh > tritone.
musical_example: Root of fifth (C-G) is the lower note C; root of fourth (G-C) is the upper note C according to acoustic interval inversion.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Perceptual dissonance ranking depends on register, timbre, and harmonic context.

citation_reference: MMA (1996), Table 1, p. 10
claim_text: MIDI 1.0 Note Numbers span 0 to 127, where 60 represents Middle C, 69 represents A4 (440 Hz), and 0 represents C-1 (8.1758 Hz).
musical_example: Octave 4 spans MIDI 60 (C4) to 71 (B4).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Octave labeling conventions vary between DAWs (Yamaha uses C3=60, Roland uses C4=60).

claim_text: MIDI Pitch Bend uses a 14-bit unsigned integer (0-16383) with 8192 (0x2000) representing center (no bend).
musical_example: Default range of +/- 2 semitones: bend 16383 = +200 cents, bend 0 = -200 cents, 1 unit ≈ 0.0244 cents.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Semitone bend depth is determined by the receiving synthesizer pitch bend range RPN 0x0000.

citation_reference: Müller (2015), Ch. 3, p. 78
claim_text: Cent deviation delta between an arbitrary frequency f and equal tempered frequency f_TET is calculated as delta_cents = 1200 * log2(f / f_TET).
musical_example: Pure major third (f/f0 = 5/4 = 1.25): 1200 * log2(1.25) = 386.31 cents; deviation from 400 cents is -13.69 cents.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Valid only for positive non-zero frequencies.

citation_reference: W3C MusicXML 4.0, pitch and semitones data type, https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/data-types/semitones/
claim_text: MusicXML represents pitch spelling through step, optional alter, and octave. Alter uses decimal semitones and supports fractional values.
musical_example: C#4 and Db4 have different step and alter fields. Quarter-tone examples: <alter>0.5</alter> and <alter>-0.5</alter>.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: A MIDI note number alone does not preserve written pitch spelling. A MusicXML importer must handle or explicitly reject fractional alterations.

citation_reference: Kostka & Payne (2013), Ch. 1, p. 5
claim_text: German nomenclature uses H for pitch class 11 (international B natural) and B for pitch class 10 (international B flat).
musical_example: German H-Dur = B major; German B-Dur = Bb major; German B-A-C-H motif = Bb4-A4-C5-B4.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Context language must be explicitly declared to prevent 1-semitone transposition errors.

citation_reference: Kostka & Payne (2013), Ch. 1, p. 8
claim_text: Double accidentals indicate a two-semitone shift: double sharp (x) raises pitch by 2 semitones, double flat (bb) lowers pitch by 2 semitones.
musical_example: In G# harmonic minor, leading tone to G# is Fx (F double sharp, MIDI 67, pitch class 7). Writing G natural is grammatically invalid.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: In 12-TET, Fx is enharmonically equivalent to G natural, but scale spelling requires step F.

citation_reference: Alfred (1994), p. 4
claim_text: Circle of fifths key signature order is strictly deterministic: Sharps follow F#-C#-G#-D#-A#-E#-B#; Flats follow Bb-Eb-Ab-Db-Gb-Cb-Fb.
musical_example: Key of E major has 4 sharps: F#, C#, G#, D#. Key of Ab major has 4 flats: Bb, Eb, Ab, Db.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Irregular modal signatures (e.g. D Dorian written with 0 flats instead of 1 flat with B natural accidentals) follow alternative conventions.

citation_reference: Kostka & Payne (2013), Ch. 2, p. 28
claim_text: Scientific Pitch Notation (SPN) designates Middle C as C4 (MIDI 60), octave 4 spanning C4 to B4. Octave numbers increment at C, not at A.
musical_example: B3 (MIDI 59) is immediately followed by C4 (MIDI 60).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Helmholtz notation uses c' for C4 and c for C3; MIDI manufacturers occasionally use C3 for 60.

citation_reference: Oliver Prehn, The Modes, pp. 1–2, https://newjazz.dk/Compendiums/Major_Melmi_Harmmi_HarmMa_Modes.pdf. Former attribution to SRC-033 unconfirmed.
claim_text: The major, ascending melodic minor, harmonic minor and harmonic major scales yield 28 distinct cyclic interval patterns when each of their seven degrees is used as the starting point.
musical_example: D Dorian is a major mode. C Altered is a mode of Db ascending melodic minor. A harmonic minor contains a three-semitone step from F to G#.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The count applies to these four selected families. It does not enumerate all seven-note collections in 12-TET.

citation_reference: Levine (1995), Ch. 5, p. 58
claim_text: The Altered Scale (Super Locrian) is the 7th mode of Melodic Minor, containing formula 1, b2, b3, b4, b5, b6, b7 (enharmonically 1, b9, #9, 3, b5/#11, #5/b13, b7).
musical_example: C Altered scale: C, Db, D#, E, F#, G#, Bb. Derived from Db Melodic Minor (Db, Eb, Fb, Gb, Ab, Bb, C).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Requires dominant seventh context with altered tensions; incompatible with natural 5th or natural 9th.

citation_reference: Levine (1995), Ch. 6, p. 74
claim_text: Lydian Dominant is the 4th mode of Melodic Minor, possessing interval formula 1, 2, 3, #4, 5, 6, b7 (or 1, 9, 3, #11, 5, 13, b7).
musical_example: G Lydian Dominant: G, A, B, C#, D, E, F. 4th mode of D Melodic Minor (D, E, F, G, A, B, C#). Used on tritone substitutes and unresolving dominants (II7).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Avoids the natural 11th (C natural), replacing it with the raised fourth #11 (C#).

claim_text: The Bebop Dominant scale adds a passing major seventh between the b7 and the root of the Mixolydian scale, creating an 8-note scale.
musical_example: G Bebop Dominant: G, A, B, C, D, E, F, F#, G. Ensures chord tones (G, B, D, F) fall on downbeats when played in eighth notes.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Chromatic passing tone F# is unaccented; on downbeat it clashes functionally with root.

citation_reference: Persichetti (1961), Ch. 2, p. 44
claim_text: The Octatonic (Diminished) scale alternates whole and half steps, possessing only three unique transpositional collections in 12-TET.
musical_example: Half-Whole diminished on C: C, Db, Eb, E, F#, G, A, Bb. Whole-Half on C: C, D, Eb, F, F#, G#, A, B.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Symmetric structure lacks a unique diatonic tonic; tonality is defined by local bass assertion.

claim_text: Rootless jazz voicings omit the root (delegated to bass player) and are categorized into A-type (voicing 3-5-7-9 from bottom) and B-type (voicing 7-9-3-5 from bottom).
musical_example: Cmaj9: A-type = [E3, G3, B3, D4]; B-type = [B3, D4, E4, G4]. Dm9: A-type = [F3, A3, C4, E4]; B-type = [C4, E4, F4, A4].
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Rootless voicings sound hollow or ambiguous without an acoustic bass instrument providing the root.

citation_reference: Persichetti (1961), Ch. 6, p. 135
claim_text: Polychords consist of two distinct triads or seventh chords sounded simultaneously, separated by pitch register and notated with a horizontal bar (D/C).
musical_example: D over C triad [C, E, G | D, F#, A] forms acoustic polychord Cmaj13(#11). Slash notation D/C specifies D triad with C single bass note.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: If voices interlock in the same octave, the ear hears a single complex tertian extension rather than a polychord.

citation_reference: Open Music Theory, Chord Symbols, Bass notes, https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/chord-symbols/ Historical reference: Kostka & Payne (2013), Ch. 3, p. 45 (unverified).
claim_text: For a known triad or seventh chord, a chord tone in the bass determines its position or inversion. A slash bass can also be a nonchord tone.
musical_example: C/E is first inversion; C/G is second inversion; C/F# is a C-major triad over a nonchord bass.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: This assumes the chord identity is established. Bass alone does not identify the chord.

claim_text: Upper structure triads on dominant seventh chords are major or minor triads built on extensions that contain no avoid notes.
musical_example: A major triad over C7 [C-E-G-Bb + A-C#-E] creates C7(b9, 13). F# major triad over C7 [C-E-G-Bb + F#-A#-C#] creates C7(b9, #11).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Upper structure triads must omit the natural 4th/11th to avoid clashing with the chord 3rd.

citation_reference: Harrison (1998), Ch. 2, p. 18
claim_text: Suspended chords (sus4) replace the third with the perfect fourth [0, 5, 7], creating open harmonic tension that does not establish major or minor modality.
musical_example: Csus4 = [C, F, G]. Cadd9 retains the third [C, D, E, G]; Csus2 replaces the third with the second [C, D, G].
falsification_or_boundary_condition: If fourth and third are played simultaneously in close position, the fourth is an added 11th, not a sus chord.

citation_reference: Aldwell & Schachter (2011), Ch. 31, p. 552
claim_text: Secondary dominant V7/V (II7) resolves deceptively to ii7 over an identical root via a chromatic half-step descent of the major third to the minor third.
musical_example: In C major: D7 [D, F#, A, C] moves to Dm7 [D, F, A, C], with F# descending to F natural. D7 is V7/V (NOT V7/ii).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: V7/ii in C major is A7 resolving to Dm. Labeling D7 as V7/ii is a functional error (ERR-033).

citation_reference: Spencer (1996), Ch. 12, p. 210
claim_text: Modal interchange (borrowing) imports chords from the parallel minor into a major key: bIII, iv, bVI, and bVII without abandoning major tonicity.
musical_example: In C major: Fm (iv), Abmaj7 (bVI), and Bb7 (bVII) borrowed from C minor. Resolves smoothly to Cmaj7.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: If borrowed chords establish independent tonic confirmation via new dominant-tonic cadences, the music has modulated.

citation_reference: Open Music Theory, Substitutions, Key Takeaways and Tritone Substitutions, https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/substitutions/ Historical reference: Levine (1995), Ch. 18, p. 295 (unverified).
claim_text: Tritone substitution can replace a dominant seventh with another dominant seventh whose root is a tritone away. Their third and seventh exchange roles as pitch classes.
musical_example: G7 spells G–B–D–F. Db7 spells Db–F–Ab–Cb. The shared pitch classes are F and B/Cb.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The pitch-class match assumes 12-TET. Whether the replacement fits depends on the local melody, bass and dominant context.

citation_reference: Spencer (1996), Ch. 14, p. 245
claim_text: Chromatic mediants are chords whose roots are related by a major or minor third, belong to the same chord quality (both major or both minor), and share one common tone.
musical_example: C major to E major: share common tone E; C and G move by half-step to B and G#. C major to Ab major: share common tone C; E and G move to Eb and Ab.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Diatonic mediants (C to Em or Am) share two common tones and differ in quality; chromatic mediants share only one common tone.

citation_reference: Kostka & Payne (2013), Ch. 18, p. 312
claim_text: Pivot chord modulation shifts tonal center via a diatonic chord common to both the initial and target keys, functioning simultaneously in both.
musical_example: Modulation from C major to G major: C (I) -> Am (vi in C = ii in G) -> D7 (V7 in G) -> G (I in G). Am is the pivot chord.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Does not apply to direct / abrupt modulations where the new key begins without an overlapping diatonic link.

citation_reference: Aldwell & Schachter (2011), Ch. 5, p. 82
claim_text: Voice-leading smoothness is quantified by L1 distance in semitones: minimal total voice displacement between adjacent chord tones produces optimal voice leading.
musical_example: C [C4, E4, G4] to G/B [B3, D4, G4]: C4->B3 (1 st), E4->D4 (2 st), G4->G4 (0 st). Total L1 distance = 3 semitones.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Parallel octaves/fifths restrictions override pure L1 minimization in classical counterpoint.

citation_reference: Open Music Theory, ii–V–I, Example 2 and the preceding paragraph, https://viva.pressbooks.pub/openmusictheory/chapter/ii-v-i/. Historical reference: Levine (1995), Ch. 2, p. 24, page unverified.
claim_text: In a C-major ii–V–I with Dm7–G7–Cmaj7, the voices C4–B3 and F4–E4 descend by semitone. In the minor example Dm7b5–G7–Cm7, C4–B3 remains a semitone while F4–Eb4 descends by a whole tone.
musical_example: Major: Dm7 (C4) to G7 (B3) and G7 (F4) to Cmaj7 (E4). Minor: Dm7b5 (C4) to G7 (B3) and G7 (F4) to Cm7 (Eb4).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: These examples describe particular voices and chord qualities. A different voicing or tonic quality can lead to a different motion.

citation_reference: Linn (1988), MPC3000 Manual, p. 42
claim_text: At 480 PPQ, 61% 16th-note swing quantizes the second sixteenth of a 240-tick span to Tick 146 (round(240 * 0.61) = round(146.4) = 146), an offset of +26 ticks (36.11 ms at 90 BPM).
musical_example: Straight 16th pair = [0, 120]; 61% swung pair = [0, 146]. Tick delta = +26 ticks.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Claiming 145 ticks corresponds to 60.42% swing, NOT 61% swing (ERR-034 correction).

citation_reference: Friberg & Sundström (2002), Music Perception 19(3), 333–349, Abstract, https://doi.org/10.1525/mp.2002.19.3.333
claim_text: In the recordings studied, drummers’ ride-cymbal swing ratios generally decreased as tempo increased.
musical_example: The abstract reports ratios up to 3.5:1 at slow tempos and down to 1:1 at fast tempos.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: The sample comprises three jazz recordings and one play-along recording. The abstract does not support universal ratios for specific BPM values. Check the measurements before citing individual BPM values.

citation_reference: DeSantis (2017), Ableton Rhythm, Sec. 3
claim_text: Additive meter 5/8 is subdivided into asymmetrical beats of 3+2 (dotted quarter + quarter) or 2+3 (quarter + dotted quarter); 7/8 is subdivided into 2+2+3, 3+2+2, or 2+3+2.
musical_example: Constructed examples: 5/8 grouped 3+2 eighth notes and 7/8 grouped 2+2+3 eighth notes. Take Five uses 5/4. The main riff of Money is commonly notated in 7/4.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Treating 5/8 or 7/8 as equal-length pulses contradicts perceptual metric grouping.

citation_reference: Mauleón (1993), Ch. 3, p. 52
claim_text: 3:2 Son Clave at 480 PPQ in 4/4 meter places hits at Ticks 0, 720, 1440 in Bar 1 (3-side) and Ticks 2400 (relative 480), 2880 (relative 960) in Bar 2 (2-side).
musical_example: Total 2-bar duration = 3840 ticks. Clave hits = [0, 720, 1440, 2400, 2880].
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Confusing measure-relative ticks (480, 960) with continuous timeline ticks (2400, 2880) causes sequencing errors.

citation_reference: MMA GM 1.0 (1996), Channel 10 Map
claim_text: General MIDI 1.0 defines fixed drum percussion mappings on Channel 10: Bass Drum (35/36), Side Stick (37), Acoustic Snare (38), Hand Clap (39), Closed Hat (42), Pedal Hat (44), Open Hat (46), Ride (51), Cowbell (56).
musical_example: Standard kit triggers kick on 36, snare on 38, closed hat on 42.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Extended GM2 or proprietary vendor drum maps (e.g. Roland GS, Yamaha XG) add notes but preserve core 35-56.

citation_reference: UFRJ, Rhythmic Analysis and Modeling of Expressive Music Performances, p. 42 and Fig. 2.17. Historical comparison: Schreiner (1993), p. 95, not checked.
claim_text: In the samba-enredo pattern described by the UFRJ study, surdo de primeira or marcação marks beat 2 and surdo de segunda or resposta marks beat 1 in 2/4.
musical_example: Two-beat illustration: resposta on 1 and marcação on 2.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Instrumentation and roles can vary between samba schools. This example does not prescribe accents for bossa nova.

citation_reference: Schreiner (1993), Ch. 6, p. 142
claim_text: João Gilberto created the Bossa Nova batida by synthesizing the Samba percussion section (Tamborim syncopations in right hand, Surdo bass in thumb) onto the classical guitar.
musical_example: Bossa comping delays the second hit of the 2-side to beat 3+ (Tick 1200 relative / 3120 absolute).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Bossa batida is historically Brazilian; calling it Cuban Son Clave is an academic misclassification.

citation_reference: Mauleón (1993), Ch. 5, p. 110
claim_text: In Afro-Cuban Salsa and Son, the Montuno (Guajeo) piano pattern is an arpeggiated ostinato that anticipates chord changes by landing on beat 4 or 4+.
musical_example: Over Cm - Fm - G7 - Fm vamp, piano arpeggiates octaves locked to 2:3 or 3:2 clave.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Montuno is an instrumental performance figure, not a harmonic progression.

citation_reference: Alfred (1994), p. 12
claim_text: Standard piano scale fingerings for C major: Right hand 1-2-3-1-2-3-4-5; Left hand 5-4-3-2-1-3-2-1, crossing thumb after third and fourth fingers.
musical_example: Ascending RH C4: 1(C), 2(D), 3(E), thumb under to 1(F), 2(G), 3(A), 4(B), 5(C5).
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Black-key starting scales (e.g. F# major, Bb major) use modified fingerings to keep thumb off black keys.

claim_text: Drop-2 voicings lower the second voice from the top of a close-position four-note seventh chord by one octave into the left hand or lower register.
musical_example: Close Dm7 [D4, F4, A4, C5]: drop 2nd voice A4 down to A3 -> [A3 | D4, F4, C5]. Expands voicing span and improves acoustic clarity.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Drop-2 requires four-voice tertian chords; does not apply to triads or five-note voicings.

citation_reference: W3C MusicXML 4.0, time-modification and tuplet, https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/time-modification/ and https://www.w3.org/2021/06/musicxml40/musicxml-reference/elements/tuplet/
claim_text: MusicXML time-modification gives the sounding ratio with actual-notes and normal-notes. The tuplet notation element provides graphical start/stop and grouping details.
musical_example: actual-notes 7 and normal-notes 4 encode seven written units in the time normally taken by four. The tuplet element can show a bracket.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Standard MIDI Files carry timing and do not encode the MusicXML notation elements.

citation_reference: MMA MIDI 1.0 (1996), Standard MIDI Files 1.0, p. 3
claim_text: Standard MIDI Files (SMF) define division in the header chunk as positive integer PPQ (pulses per quarter note) or negative SMPTE frame format.
musical_example: Header chunk MThd with division 0x01E0 = 480 PPQ; 0x03C0 = 960 PPQ.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Delta times in MIDI tracks are variable-length quantities (VLQ), not fixed 32-bit integers.

claim_text: Functional bass ear training teaches students to identify progressions by tracking the lowest acoustic pitch movement (I-IV-V) before deciphering upper-voice extensions.
musical_example: Hearing bass drop a fifth (G to C) identifies dominant resolution regardless of whether upper voices play G7, G9, G13, or G7alt.
falsification_or_boundary_condition: Inversions (e.g. I6/4 or V6/5) disguise the root; students must combine bass listening with guide-tone checking.
